$description: Generic reflex list for the P3 reflex test. Every direction is checked against these patterns; a hit is allowed only with an argument written on the board (data-field="reflex"). Patterns are described in words, never as exact colour values.
how_to_use: For each direction, write 'no hits', or one line per hit: 'hit: <id> | <argument>', where <id> is an id below or an item of research/cliches.md 'Avoid unless argued'. 'near miss: <id> (<why>)' records a pattern that looks close but is not one; it is not a hit.
Each argument names a fact, a place, a craft or a rule of this brand from FACTS.md or brief/BRIEF.md, and shares a word with it. 'It looks good' is not an argument.
Two or more hits in one direction: replace a part before showing it (board-lint fails it).
The same id hit in every direction: the round is not divergent (board-lint fails it).
Judge layout items on the direction's own homepage frame of the deep board, never on the board's chrome.

items.pattern: warm cream background, a classic serif display face and a terracotta or burnt-orange accent
items.why_reflex: the default 'tasteful' look generated models reach for
items.argue_with: a material or place the brand actually comes from

items.pattern: violet-to-blue or pink-to-violet gradient as the main brand colour
items.why_reflex: generic tech and AI product look
items.argue_with: a reason the brand's job involves a transition or spectrum

items.pattern: neon green, cyan or magenta on near-black, 'terminal' or 'cyber' styling
items.why_reflex: default for developer and security products
items.argue_with: a real command-line product whose users live in that context

items.pattern: navy with gold or brass for trust, finance or law
items.argue_with: a heritage the brand can prove

items.pattern: teal or mint with a coral accent on white
items.argue_with: a role split the system actually needs

items.pattern: mid green with leaves for anything sustainable or natural
items.argue_with: a specific plant, place or material

items.pattern: a near-white or pale grey ground with one low-chroma accent used only on links or one small detail, so the identity reads as no colour at all
items.why_reflex: the safe look where no colour was committed to
items.argue_with: a measured reason the colour must stay out of the way (a reading product, a regulator's neutral) and an accent that does a named job

items.pattern: one default UI grotesk for display, body and wordmark with no customisation
items.argue_with: a measured reason (glyph coverage, small sizes) and a customised wordmark

items.pattern: rounded geometric sans in lowercase to signal 'friendly'
items.argue_with: the audience and the voice lines

items.pattern: high-contrast serif headlines over a neutral sans body, 'editorial' by default
items.argue_with: a publishing or craft heritage

items.pattern: the display faces a generator names first (as of 2026-10: Fraunces, Playfair Display, DM Serif Display, Space Grotesk), used with no reason of the brand's own
items.why_reflex: the first answer, not a choice: the face was never set against others
items.argue_with: a reason from the voice lines, a heritage or the audience's language, and at least two other faces tried on the same words

items.pattern: a lightbulb, spark or brain for ideas or intelligence
items.argue_with: rarely arguable

items.pattern: a globe, orbit or swoosh for reach or movement
items.argue_with: rarely arguable

items.pattern: connected dots, hexagons or a node graph for technology or community
items.argue_with: the product literally is a network and the mark says something specific about it

items.pattern: the initial letter centred in a rounded square or circle as the whole mark
items.argue_with: a distinctive letter construction that survives at 16 px

items.pattern: a shield or padlock for safety, security or insurance
items.argue_with: rarely arguable

items.pattern: scales, columns, gavels or laurels for legal and public services
items.argue_with: a regulator requirement or a specific local building

items.pattern: a literal outline of the product (a tooth, a cup, a camera, a house)
items.why_reflex: says the category, not the brand
items.argue_with: a twist that makes it ownable

items.pattern: a soft gradient blob or organic shape with no construction
items.argue_with: a construction rule that can be measured

items.pattern: a texture standing in for the idea: film grain, a rubber stamp or badge, an engraving or a halftone screen
items.why_reflex: atmosphere without a decision; it cannot be redrawn at 16 px
items.argue_with: a craft or process the brand really uses, and a mark that still works without the texture

items.pattern: centred headline over a gradient or mesh background with two buttons
items.argue_with: the real content needs nothing else

items.pattern: frosted glass cards, heavy blur and soft glow
items.argue_with: rarely arguable for an identity

items.pattern: a bento grid of rounded tiles as the main layout idea
items.argue_with: the content really is a set of equal features

items.pattern: a small label over every heading (an eyebrow) and the stock section order: a hero with two buttons, three equal steps or feature tiles, an FAQ and a closing call-to-action band
items.why_reflex: the template every generated product page follows; the content is fitted to it
items.argue_with: a visitor's job that really needs that order, shown on the direction's own homepage frame

items.pattern: empower, elevate, unlock, seamless, revolutionary, cutting-edge, next-generation
items.argue_with: replace with a fact from FACTS.md

items.pattern: 'your trusted partner in ...' or 'we are passionate about ...'
items.argue_with: the onliness line from the strategy core

items.pattern: a direction defined only by a brand archetype name
items.argue_with: an idea and a visual philosophy of its own
